title: How to Find the Best Recruitment Agency in Nigeria
dek: Nigeria has no shortage of people looking for jobs. What it has a shortage of is recruitment agencies that take the vetting seriously. Choosing the wrong one costs you time, money, and the opportunity cost of an unfilled role sitting vacant while the process drags on.

sections.heading: What Most Recruitment Agencies in Nigeria Actually Do
paragraphs: The majority of recruitment agencies in Nigeria operate the same way: they receive a job brief, search their database or post on job boards, collect CVs, and send you a batch. The vetting, if any, is minimal. You end up interviewing ten people and not finding anyone that actually fits your company, and then you are told your placement window has expired.

This is expensive in ways that do not appear on an invoice. The cost of a bad hire in Nigeria, accounting for lost productivity, retraining time, and the disruption to existing staff, is consistently several times the monthly salary of the role being filled.

sections.heading: What to Look For in a Nigerian Recruitment Agency
paragraphs: Good recruitment firms maintain a verified pool of vetted candidates. They do not merely start looking when you reach out to them. They maintain a community of pre-screened, ready-to-work candidates and match from that pool. This is what drives fast turnaround without sacrificing quality.

Good recruitment firms have predetermined and standardized processes for how candidates are screened. Reference checks, skills verification, background checks, and structured interviews are the minimum.

entries.q: What should I look for in a recruitment agency in Nigeria?
entries.a: Look for a verified talent pool, a structured vetting process, a clear turnaround commitment, transparent pricing, and a track record of placing candidates in roles similar to yours. Avoid agencies that send you unvetted CVs in bulk, charge high fees upfront without performance guarantees, or cannot explain how they screen candidates.
